correctness.rationale: For every fixed interior binary iid bias, greedy embedding converts each pattern to an independent geometric waiting-time product. Parikh-matched half enumeration gives the exact binomial-square series and a constant-term identity gives the algebraic bivariate generating function. Its critical root r=1/(1+sqrt(p(1-p))) is unique, nonperiodic coefficient positivity excludes other modulus-r singularities, the derivative rS'(r)=2(1+t)/(1+2t) is direct algebra, and transfer gives the stated leading constant and ratio. Four rational sources and all 8190 nonempty binary hosts of lengths at most 12 were checked using three exactly agreeing computational paths; these are supporting checks, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted primary research, scientific-web and published mathematical-record searches found no equivalent binary biased-source expected count of distinct *scattered* Abelian-square patterns with the length-refined algebraic generating function and n^(-1/2) ratio. Prior results separately count all Abelian-square strings, unrestricted random-host subsequences, and contiguous Abelian-square factors; none inspected states this result. A general weighted-language composition theorem could subsume it, which remains a documented residual risk.
residual_risks: No independent mathematical priority check has been performed.

The classical ingredients make independent rediscovery relatively plausible; the new claimed scope is precisely the combined expectation and constant.

value.rationale: This computes an unaddressed natural expected complexity invariant for a classical pattern family; the central mathematical fact is that a language constraint preserving the unrestricted exponential base nevertheless enforces an exact inverse-square-root proportion. The entire length spectrum, continuous bias dependence of the constant, unique fair-source rate maximizer and discontinuous deterministic-source boundary are resolved for infinitely many host lengths. The claim is not a finite table, trivial relabeling, or asserted application unsupported by the theorem.
